title: Removing objects from a child's ear or nose
what: An ENT doctor (ear, nose, and throat doctor) gently removes the object from your child's ear or nose with a special tool.
why: When a child pushes a bead, a toy, or food into the nose or ear, or an insect gets in.
tell_doctor: If you tried to remove it at home
If there is blood, discharge, or pain

prepare.title: Do not remove it yourself
prepare.text: Do not try to get it out with tweezers or a cotton swab. You can push it deeper.

prepare.title: Battery
prepare.text: If it is a button battery or a magnet, go to a doctor immediately.

prepare.title: Your child
prepare.text: Calm your child. Say the doctor will help quickly.

steps: The doctor looks into the nose or ear with a light
Your child sits on your lap and is held so they do not move
Sometimes drops are put in the nose
The doctor removes the object with small forceps, a hook, or by rinsing
The doctor checks that nothing is left behind
feel: Your child may be scared and uncomfortable and may cry
It is usually quick. Comfort and praise your child
after: Sometimes there is a little blood from the nose. It stops
Keep small objects away from children
red_flags: A battery in the nose or ear: see a doctor right away or call emergency services
Your child is coughing, choking, or wheezing: call emergency services
Severe pain, blood, or pus afterward
A bad smell from one side of the nose: see a doctor

faq.a: Only if the object is visible and comes out easily. Otherwise, see a doctor. You can push it deeper.
It quickly burns the tissue. Urgent help is needed.

reminders.text: Do not try to remove the object yourself. Go to the ENT doctor.
